Probably not—at least not with normal unaided eyesight under those conditions.

The Moon is technically above the horizon, but it is a very thin crescent: only **11.39% illuminated**, and it is about **39° from the Sun**. With the Sun 34° high and the Moon 18° high, the Moon is in bright daytime sky, where atmospheric scattering greatly reduces contrast. Its separation from the Sun is also modest, so the sky around it is especially bright.

A crescent at roughly 11% illumination can sometimes be seen in daylight, particularly with binoculars or exceptionally clear, dry air. But from Reykjavík in bright daylight, with ordinary eyesight and no precise pointing aid, it would be **very difficult and probably effectively invisible**. It is not geometrically impossible to see—the Moon is above the horizon and sufficiently separated from the Sun—but your “impossible to see right now” wish is close to reality for unaided observation.

If attempting it, use the app to point very precisely, avoid looking anywhere near the Sun, and use binoculars only after the Moon’s position is safely established.
